explanation: In C, an array is a fixed-size collection of elements of the same data type stored in contiguous memory locations. It is used to efficiently store and access multiple related values, such as a list of numbers, simplifying data management and iteration in programs.
example_explanation: This program declares an integer array 'a' with 10 elements, assigns the value 1 to the element at index 0 (a[0]), and prints it to the console. This demonstrates how arrays are declared, elements are accessed via indexing, and values are stored and retrieved in contiguous memory, illustrating the basic concept of arrays in C.
